text: {"headline":"Provider 1000000010 bills 99215 well above expectation at every complexity level, including low-complexity patients, but records are too thin to confirm or rule out upcoding.","leaning":"inconclusive","interpretation":"The 99215 share runs roughly two to three times the all-provider rate in every complexity band, including patients with zero or one chronic condition. The sampled low-complexity 99215 claims are mostly single, simple diagnoses such as rash (R21), abdominal pain (R10.9) or follow-up (Z09), for example C0003475, C0003855 and C0005250, which is the pattern most consistent with upcoding. Against that, the provider's panel does skew complex, and the sampled high-complexity 99215 claims (for example C0003714 and C0004382) look clinically plausible. The only two documented 99215 claims (C0003750 and C0003867) support high MDM, which is far too few to judge either way. The 99214 claims show a modestly elevated unsupported rate (C0003446, C0005118), and only 2 of the 24 notes claiming moderate-or-higher data review lacked a lab or test line, so there is little sign of cloned notes. A reviewer should first request charts for the low-complexity 99215 claims, starting with the R21, R10.9 and Z09 visits listed here, and should also pull more 99214 records to see whether the unsupported rate holds up."}
